title: Uniformly continuous ring homomorphisms extend along dense isometric embeddings
statement: Let $A,B,C$ be fields [def-weil-field], each equipped with a metric whose topology makes addition and multiplication continuous. Suppose $C$ is complete, meaning every Cauchy sequence in $C$ converges. Let $i:A\to B$ and $h:A\to C$ be unital ring homomorphisms. Assume $d_B(i(a),i(a'))=d_A(a,a')$ for all $a,a'\in A$, that every open ball in $B$ meets $i(A)$, and that $h$ is uniformly continuous. Then there is a uniformly continuous unital ring homomorphism $T:B\to C$ satisfying $T(i(a))=h(a)$ for every $a\in A$. Uniform continuity means that for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that input distance less than $\delta$ implies output distance less than $\epsilon$, independently of the input points.

Metric spaces are Hausdorff. No completeness of A or B is required.
